source.citation: Elakneswaran, Y., Nawa, T., Kurumisawa, K. (2009). Electrokinetic potential of hydrated cement in relation to adsorption of chlorides. Cement and Concrete Research 39(4), 340-344.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF), pp. 341-343, read on the page text
transcription.note: The deprotonation is written against OH-, Eq. (1), and its constant, -12.7, is set beside -12.3 (Viallis-Terrisse et al.) and -12.0 (Pointeau et al.), which are constants of the proton form >SOH = >SO- + H+; the three are compared as values of one quantity. The calcium constant, -9.4, is compared the same way with -9.4 and -9.2.

specific_surface_area.description: Specific surface area assumed for C-S-H.

area_per_two_sites.description: Area, in Å2, occupied by three silicate tetrahedra carrying two negative charges when fully dissociated, after Viallis-Terrisse et al.: two sites on 41 Å2.

surface_reactions.location: pp. 342-343: constants fitted to zeta potentials

notes: Eqs. (5) and (6) add the ternary complexes ≡SiOCaSO4- and ≡SiOCaCl, without a constant in the text.
Two sites on 41 Å2 with 500 m2/g give 4.05e-3 mol of sites per gram, the density Pointeau et al. and Guo et al. use.
